fc_summary: John "Jack" Prip (1922–2009) was a Danish-trained, fourth-generation metalsmith, a founding member of the Society of North American Goldsmiths, and a longtime RISD professor (1963–1981); he died in 2009 in Providence, RI.

name: ELLIOT PUJOL
fc_current_role: Emeritus Professor of Metalsmithing & Jewelry, Department of Art, Kansas State University (retired 2013)

He built the KSU metalsmithing/jewelry program from 1973, entered phased retirement in 2010, and fully retired in 2013; he is now Emeritus Professor. No obituary found; he was actively making work as of 2018 and is very likely still living.

name: ARTHUR PULOS

fc_summary: Arthur J. Pulos (1917–1997), silversmith, industrial designer, design historian, and longtime Syracuse University design professor (retired 1982); died January 15, 1997.

fc_summary: Robert "Bob" Pum, a founding member of the UW–Green Bay art department (1969) who taught art metals/jewelry, retired in 1998 as Professor Emeritus and died December 7, 2019, at age 83.

name: ROBIN QUIGLEY

name: SVETOZAR RADAKOVICH
fc_current_role: Independent studio metalsmith/jeweler and sculptor in Encinitas, CA (with wife Ruth Clark Radakovich); deceased 1998. Earlier taught/studied at the School for American Craftsmen, Rochester, NY.

He is a historical figure celebrated as a pioneer of lost-wax/centrifugal casting in American art jewelry.

name: CHRIS RAMSAY

fc_summary: Chris (Christopher Theodore) Ramsay, the metals/jewelry artist and OSU professor, taught at Oklahoma State University from 1990 to 2023 (retiring as Professor Emeritus) and died January 24, 2026 at age 64.

name: CAMILLE RENDAL
fc_current_role: Adjunct/art professor teaching jewelry-metals, art history, drawing/painting at several Washington & New Mexico community/technical colleges (e.g., Clover Park Technical College, Columbia Basin College, Renton Technical College, Front Range Community College, Santa Fe Community College); independent artist (jewelry line "RavenSaint")
fc_summary: Camille Rendal (b. 1955) is alive and actively teaching as of 2024-2025; the metalsmith/painter with an NMSU MFA and Otis Parsons BFA now teaches art at several Washington and New Mexico community/technical colleges and makes jewelry under the brand "RavenSaint." Her name is unchanged.

name: MERRY RENK

She died June 17, 2012, in San Francisco. The archived education record (Trenton School of Industrial Arts; Institute of Design, Chicago) is confirmed accurate.

name: RICHARD REINHARDT

name: ALAN REVERE
fc_current_role: Retired founder/director of the Revere Academy of Jewelry Arts (San Francisco), which he ran 1979-2017; now a goldsmith/educator who consults with GIA and leads the "Let's Make Professional Jewelry" online community.
fc_summary: Alan Revere is alive and active. He closed the Revere Academy of Jewelry Arts in December 2017 after 40 years and retired from running the school; he continues as a goldsmith/educator (GIA consulting, online teaching community, ongoing jewelry design).

name: LINDA L. RYAN
fc_current_role: Instructor Emeritus, Art (jewelry/metals), Casper College — emeritus status granted 2017
fc_summary: Linda Ryan taught jewelry/metals in the Fine Arts department at Casper College from 1982; she retired and was granted Instructor Emeritus in Art status in 2017. She is no longer on the active Visual Arts faculty.

name: GINNA SADLER
fc_current_role: Professor Emeritus of Art and Design, Abilene Christian University (taught 1980-2016)
fc_summary: Ginna Sadler (Virginia "Ginna" Joyce Gustafson Sadler), a jeweler/metalsmith and longtime ACU art professor, taught at Abilene Christian University from 1980 until retiring in 2016 as professor emeritus; she died March 12, 2023, at age 74.

name: JOHN E. SATTERFIELD
fc_current_role: Professor of metals/jewelry, East Carolina University School of Art and Design (1967-2000); deceased in office
fc_summary: John E. Born 1931, University of Kansas MFA (studied under Carlyle Smith). No name change.

name: MARY ANN SCHERR

name: MAJORIE SCHICK
fc_current_role: Professor of Art (jewelry/metalsmithing), Pittsburg State University, Kansas (1967–2017); retired 2017
fc_summary: Marjorie Schick (the archived "Majorie" is a misspelling) was a pioneering art-jewelry artist who taught at Pittsburg State University from 1967 until retiring in 2017; she died December 17, 2017 at age 76.

No evidence of a name change or death.

fc_summary: Enzo Torcoletti (b. 1943) is alive and active; he taught at Flagler College from 1971 and is now Emeritus Professor of Art there (retired from full-time teaching ~2007), continuing as an independent sculptor in St. Augustine and Italy.

name: SAMUEL YELLIN
fc_current_role: Master blacksmith/metalworker and founder of Samuel Yellin Metalworkers, Philadelphia; taught at the Pennsylvania Museum School of Industrial Art (1906–1919). Deceased.
fc_summary: Samuel Yellin (1885–1940) was a renowned American master ironworker/metalsmith and founder of Samuel Yellin Metalworkers in Philadelphia, who taught at the Pennsylvania Museum School of Industrial Art from 1906 to 1919. He died in 1940; this is a historical figure, not a current educator.

name: NORMA YOUNG LATTA
fc_current_role: Formerly associated with Oral Roberts University art program (Tulsa, OK); co-author/artist of "Faces of Truth" (2011) with husband Doug Latta. No current faculty listing found; given 1942 birth year, almost certainly retired/emeritus.
fc_summary: Norma Latta (Tulsa, OK) is confirmed as the directory subject via an exact education match — BS in Art Education from East Carolina University and MA from George Peabody College at Vanderbilt — and her Oral Roberts University connection (her husband Doug Latta directed ORU's commercial art program). She was alive and active as a co-author/artist as recently as 2013; current alive status and exact present role are unknown, but retired/emeritus is most likely given her 1942 birth year.

name: CLAUS BURY
fc_current_role: Sculptor and goldsmith based in Frankfurt am Main; former professor at Bergische Universität Wuppertal (from 1987) and Akademie der Bildenden Künste Nürnberg (2003–2011)
fc_summary: Claus Bury (b. 29 March 1946, Gelnhausen-Meerholz) is alive — the city of Hanau issued an 80th-birthday tribute dated 29 March 2026. The German goldsmith-turned-art-jeweler became an internationally significant sculptor of monumental public works; he lives and works in Frankfurt am Main.

name: EARL KRENTZIN
fc_current_role: Self-employed silver sculptor / metalsmith, Detroit / Grosse Pointe Farms, Michigan (1961-1964, 1967-2021)
fc_summary: Earl Krentzin was a noted American silver sculptor and metalsmith (Wayne State BFA 1952, Cranbrook MFA 1954) who died February 2, 2021, at age 91. His name never changed; he was a self-employed studio artist, not a teaching faculty member (consistent with the archived "n/a" teaching status).

name: KOMELIA OKIM
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita of Art (Metals & Crafts), Montgomery College, Rockville, MD (retired 2014)
fc_summary: Komelia Hongja Okim (b. 1939, Seoul) taught metals/crafts at Montgomery College 1972-2014 and retired as Professor Emerita; she remained active through 2019-2020 (published "Korean Metal Art" in 2019, lectures/workshops) and is categorized by Wikipedia as a living person. No obituary found.

name: LINDA THREADGILL
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita, University of Wisconsin-Whitewater (led the Metals Program 1979-2003); now an independent studio artist/metalsmith in Santa Fe, New Mexico
fc_summary: Linda Threadgill (b. 1947) is alive and active; she retired from University of Wisconsin-Whitewater as Professor Emerita (headed its Metals Program 1979-2003) and now works as a studio metalsmith/jeweler in Santa Fe, New Mexico. Name unchanged.

name: PATRICE CASE
currently_at: State University of New York - Geneseo since ?
fc_current_role: Associate Professor Emerita of Studio Art (Jewelry/Metalsmithing), SUNY Geneseo
fc_summary: Patrice (E.) Case is the metalsmith/jeweler from the archived record — an Associate Professor of Studio Art at SUNY Geneseo known for her rare work with niello, with an MFA from the University of Arizona and an Indiana University background. She has since retired; she now appears on the SUNY Geneseo emeritus roster. No name change and no obituary found.

name: RUTH PENNINGTON
fc_current_role: Professor of metalwork/jewelry, University of Washington School of Art (retired); also director of the Henry Gallery and founder of the Fidalgo Summer School of Allied Arts
fc_summary: Ruth Penington (correctly spelled with one 'n', not 'Pennington' as archived) was a pioneering American jeweler/metalsmith and longtime University of Washington art faculty member; she lived 1905-1998 and is deceased.

name: DONALD DUNCAN
fc_current_role: Most likely identification: the Don/Donald Duncan described as "former Professor of Art Education at The Ohio State University" and a premier Central Ohio goldsmith/jeweler who mentored Columbus jewelers (Jack Seibert, William Weidinger). His link to Capital University is not directly confirmed in any source found; he is documented at OSU. If the same man, he would now be long retired/emeritus. Possibly deceased (see notes).
fc_summary: Likely the late-career Columbus-area goldsmith and former OSU Professor of Art Education "Don Duncan," who mentored jewelers Jack Seibert and William Weidinger; his specific tie to Capital University and his current status (alive/retired/deceased) could not be confirmed from available sources.

name: Veda Beetler
fc_summary: No verifiable information could be found about Veda Beetler as a metalsmith, jeweler, or metals-arts educator. The archived directory entry was already sparse (no birth year, no education, no current teaching institution listed), and exhaustive web searches turned up no online presence under this name or any plausible spelling variant.

name: Jennifer Sholtis
fc_current_role: Last known: Assistant Professor of Art (Metals/Jewelry), Stephen F. Austin State University (hired 2003); no current position traceable. She is NOT the metals position holder today — that is Lauren McAdams Selden.
fc_summary: Jennifer (L.) Sholtis, MFA Tyler/Temple, was hired in 2003 as an assistant professor of art metals at Stephen F. Austin State University, matching the archived record; she has since left that post (the SFA metals/jewelry faculty is now Lauren McAdams Selden) and has no traceable current public presence. Whether she is still living or working in the field is unknown.

name: ALAN BURTON THOMPSON
fc_current_role: Visiting/workshop faculty (metals/jewelry), Snow Farm: The New England Craft Program, Williamsburg, Massachusetts; studio jeweler known for assemblage brooches
fc_summary: Alan Burton Thompson (b. 1956) is a studio metalsmith/jeweler known for surreal, kitsch assemblage brooches made from found-object curiosities; his work is in the Smithsonian American Art Museum collection. He has continued to teach metals/jewelry workshops as faculty at Snow Farm: The New England Craft Program in Williamsburg, MA.

name: YU-JIN CHO
fc_current_role: Retired Professor of Metal Craft (silversmithing / metal jewelry design), Department of Metal Art & Design, Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech), Seoul, Korea — held her retirement exhibition there in 2023.
fc_summary: Yu-Jin Cho (조유진), born 1957, is a Korean metalsmith/silversmith and jeweler. Her education matches the archived record exactly (Hongik University BFA and MFA, plus an MFA from the University of Texas at Austin, ~1984-87). She spent her career as a metal-craft professor at Seoul National University of Science and Technology (SeoulTech) and held her retirement exhibition there in 2023, so she is now retired/emeritus. She is alive and still exhibiting.

name: CHUNGHI CHOO
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita of Jewelry and Metal Arts, University of Iowa School of Art, Art History, and Design (taught 1968–2015)
fc_summary: Chunghi Choo (b. May 23, 1938) is alive and is now Professor Emerita at the University of Iowa, where she founded and led the jewelry/metalsmithing program from 1968 until her retirement in 2015. Cranbrook MFA (1965) confirmed; no name change.

name: JOHN M. CHURCH
fc_current_role: Retired instructor of metalsmithing/jewelry, Interlochen Arts Academy (1970–2000)
fc_summary: John M. Church taught metalsmithing, jewelry-making, and drawing at Interlochen Arts Academy from 1970 until his retirement in 2000; he died May 4, 2021, in Traverse City, Michigan.

name: SHARON CHURCH
currently_at: The Philadelphia College of Art and Design
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita, Craft + Material Studies (formerly Philadelphia College of Art), University of the Arts, Philadelphia — retired 2014 after 35 years
fc_summary: Sharon Church (professionally also Sharon Church McNabb), the studio jeweler/metalsmith who began teaching at the Philadelphia College of Art in 1979, taught there 35 years (the school became the University of the Arts), retired in 2014 as professor emerita, and died December 25, 2022 at 74.

name: HANS CHRISTENSEN
fc_current_role: Master silversmith/metalsmith and educator; held the Charlotte Fredericks Mowris Professorship in Contemporary Crafts at the School for American Crafts, Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), where he taught for ~29 years until his death in 1983.
fc_summary: Hans Christensen (Hans Jørgen Thorvald Christensen), Danish-born American master silversmith, died in a car accident on January 16, 1983. He taught metalsmithing/jewelry at RIT's School for American Crafts from 1954 until his death and is the namesake of the Society of American Silversmiths' Hans Christensen Sterling Silversmith's Award.

name: ANTONIO CIRONO
fc_current_role: Head of Teacher Training, Rhode Island School of Design (RISD); jewelry designer/metalsmith and author of a jewelry-making book (last-known/historical; deceased 1983)
fc_summary: The archived "Antonio Cirono" is a misspelling of Antonio Cirino (1888-1983), an Italian-American RISD-trained jeweler/metalsmith, painter, and educator who served as Head of Teacher Training at the Rhode Island School of Design and authored a jewelry-making book. He died November 28, 1983.

name: KENNETH C. MacBAIN
fc_current_role: Associate Professor of Art and Head of the Jewelry/Metals Concentration, New Jersey City University (since 1994)
fc_summary: Kenneth C. MacBain is alive and still teaching at New Jersey City University, where he has been since 1994, as Associate Professor of Art and Head of the Jewelry/Metals Concentration. He remains an active contemporary studio jeweler.

name: CHRISTINE CLARK
currently_at: Oregon School of Arts and Crafts
fc_current_role: Independent artist (sculpture/installation/public art) and metalsmithing educator; co-owner of Ninety-Twenty Studios, Portland OR, and member of Nine Gallery. Formerly Professor of Art and Head of the Metals Department at Oregon College of Art and Craft (formerly Oregon School of Arts and Crafts), 1983–2019.
fc_summary: Christine Clark is alive and active. She taught metals/jewelry at Oregon School of Arts and Crafts (renamed Oregon College of Art and Craft) from 1983 to 2019, heading the Metals Department 1985–2018; OCAC closed in 2019. She now works as an independent sculpture/installation artist and is co-owner of Ninety-Twenty Studios, a maker/education space in Portland.

name: THELMA COLES
fc_current_role: Professor Emeritus, Department of Art and Art History, University of Texas at Austin
fc_summary: Thelma R. Coles, the metals/jewelry educator archived at UT Austin (MA San Diego State 1978), is now listed as Professor Emeritus in UT Austin's Department of Art and Art History. No name change and no obituary found, so her living status is unknown.

name: JOE REYES APODACA
fc_current_role: Studio jeweler/metalsmith; former Head of the Metals Department, Oregon School of Arts & Crafts (OSAC), 1980–1986
fc_summary: Joe Reyes Apodaca, the RIT-trained metalsmith and studio jeweler (Tucson-born, later based in Lake Oswego, Oregon, with wife and collaborator Linda Apodaca), died April 25, 2024 at age 82. He headed the Metals Dept. at Oregon School of Arts & Crafts 1980–1986 and has work in the Smithsonian Renwick Gallery and the Museum of Arts and Design's OBJECTS: USA collection.

name: ROBERT COOGAN
fc_current_role: Retired head of the metals program, Appalachian Center for Craft, Tennessee Tech University (retired 2015 after 34 years)
fc_summary: Robert "Bob" Coogan (b. 1952), the metalsmith/jeweler/bladesmith confirmed by the archived record, founded and headed the metals program at Tennessee Tech's Appalachian Center for Craft starting 1981 and retired in 2015 after ~34 years. No name change; no credible obituary for him was found (a 2021 obit is for a different Robert Coogan born 1958), so living status is unconfirmed.

name: JOE EDWARD CORNETT
fc_current_role: Independent jeweler/metalsmith in Flagstaff, AZ; formerly taught jewelry/metals at Northern Arizona University (now retired from that role)
fc_summary: Joe Cornett Sr., a Vietnam veteran who turned to jewelry making and went on to teach jewelry/metals at Northern Arizona University, is a Flagstaff, AZ metalsmith. He appears to have retired from NAU and now exhibits independently; recent group-show coverage describes him as alive and active (age ~71).

name: LANE COULTER
fc_current_role: Co-owner of CoulterBrooks Art and Antiques gallery, Santa Fe, NM (with Jan Brooks); formerly jewelry/metals instructor at the Institute of American Indian Arts, Santa Fe, and earlier the University of Oklahoma
fc_summary: Lane Coulter (b. 1944), metalsmith/jeweler and metals-arts educator, taught jewelry at the Institute of American Indian Arts in Santa Fe; he has since left teaching and co-owns CoulterBrooks Art and Antiques gallery in Santa Fe with Jan Brooks. Name unchanged; no obituary found.

name: NANCY MEGAN CORWIN
fc_current_role: Jeweler/metalsmith and educator specializing in chasing and repoussé; adjunct instructor at Cabrillo College and Monterey Peninsula College (CA) and itinerant workshop instructor (Penland, Haystack, Arrowmont, Pratt Fine Arts Center, West Dean College UK); formerly head of Jewelry & Metals, University of Oregon (1989–1994).
fc_summary: Confirmed as the metalsmith/jeweler and author of "Chasing and Repoussé: Methods Ancient and Modern" (2009), professionally active and exhibiting through at least 2019. Her own site styles her name "Nancy Mēgan Corwin" (macron over the e) — a stylistic spelling, not a real name change.

name: KEY CORY
fc_current_role: Professor of jewelry and metalworking at Central Washington University (held ~20 years, until his death in 1994)
fc_summary: The archived "Key Cory" is a transcription/OCR error for Ken (Kenneth) Cory, the renowned art jeweler. Birth year (1943) and education (CCAC BFA, Washington State University MFA) match exactly. He died of heart failure in January 1994 at age 50; he was a longtime professor at Central Washington University, not in the archived n/a posting.

name: MARGARET CRAVER
fc_current_role: Pioneering American studio jeweler/metalsmith and arts educator; established the jewelry and metalsmithing department at the Wichita Arts Association (1935) and trained occupational therapists/art teachers in metalsmithing through Handy & Harman. No university faculty post; archived "n/a" is consistent.
fc_summary: Margret Craver (the directory's "Margaret" is a spelling variant) was a pioneering American studio jeweler, metalsmith, and enamelist (1907–2010) who studied at the University of Kansas; she died in 2010 at age 103.

name: MICHAEL CROFT
fc_current_role: Formerly Professor of Art (metals/metalsmithing), University of Arizona School of Art (hired 1972); no longer on the current faculty directory — presumed retired/emeritus.
fc_summary: Michael Flynt Croft, metalsmith/jeweler and past president of the Society of North American Goldsmiths, taught metals at the University of Arizona from 1972; he is no longer in the school's current directory, consistent with retirement. No obituary found, but his status could not be confirmed.

name: VIRGINIA WIREMAN CUTE
fc_summary: No retrievable online source documents Virginia Wireman Cute as a jeweler/metalsmith educator; her identity, current status, and any name change could not be verified. She is plausibly a mid-20th-century Philadelphia figure (Moore College BA, Univ. of Pennsylvania MFA), but nothing online confirms birth/death, role, or married/professional name change.

name: LINDA DARTY
fc_current_role: Professor of Metal Design (now likely retired/emeritus), School of Art & Design, East Carolina University; founder/director of ECU's Italy Intensives study-abroad program in Certaldo, Tuscany
fc_summary: Linda Darty is the same metalsmith/enamelist from the archived record (confirmed by the ECU/MFA and John Satterfield instructor detail). She established ECU's first enameling program in 1981, authored The Art of Enameling (2004), and later founded and directs ECU's Italy Intensives program in Tuscany, where she now lives and teaches. No obituary found; she appears to be living and active.

name: MARILYN DaSILVA
currently_at: California College of Arts and Crafts since ?
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita, Jewelry & Metal Arts Program, California College of the Arts (San Francisco/Oakland)
fc_summary: Marilyn da Silva (b. 1952), the metalsmith/enamelist known for gesso-and-colored-pencil narrative metalwork, is alive and is now Professor Emerita of the Jewelry & Metal Arts Program at California College of the Arts — the same school as the archived "California College of Arts and Crafts" (CCAC was renamed CCA in 2003), where she has taught since 1987. She is now retired/emerita rather than the active department head.

name: ELLEN ROSE-AUYONG
fc_current_role: Professor in Visual Arts (jewelry/metalsmithing/sculpture), Department of Art, University of North Dakota — retired 1999
fc_summary: Ellen Rose Auyong was a jewelry maker/metalsmith and Professor of Visual Arts at the University of North Dakota; she retired in 1999 and died March 28, 2008.

name: BEVERLY DECMAN
fc_current_role: Retired jewelry/metalsmithing instructor, Joliet Junior College (Joliet, IL). She was the longtime metalsmithing teacher there; her student Cathy Mustari succeeded her as JJC metalsmithing instructor in 2001.
fc_summary: Beverly (Bev) Decman was the longtime jewelry/metalsmithing instructor at Joliet Junior College (the archived record's institution) and is now retired/emeritus, having been succeeded by her former student Cathy Mustari around 2001. She was alive as of 2014 (listed as surviving spouse in her husband Stephen Decman's obituary); no obituary for her was found, but her current status is unconfirmed.

name: WILLIAM R. DERREVERE
fc_current_role: Retired from Tulsa Community College (taught jewelry design, sculpture, and 3-D art there ~45 years, retiring approx. 2016–2019); currently teaching jewelry design and working in the metals/jewelry studio at AHHA (Arts & Humanities Council) in Tulsa, OK. Also longtime instructor (35 years) at Ghost Ranch, NM, and runs Derrevere Designs.
fc_summary: William "Bill" R. Derrevere is alive and active as a metalsmith/jeweler. He retired around 2016–2019 after ~45 years teaching jewelry/metals at Tulsa Community College, and as of 2025 teaches jewelry design at AHHA in Tulsa and at Ghost Ranch (NM).

name: GAIL DIAL
fc_current_role: Professor of Art, Emeritus, Idaho State University (Department of Art, Pocatello). Full name on official records: Theresa Gail Dial; professor 1974-2008.
fc_summary: The archived "Gail Dial" is Theresa Gail Dial, who taught art (metals/jewelry) at Idaho State University from 1974 to 2008 and is now listed as Professor of Art, Emeritus. No obituary was found; she appears retired rather than deceased, but her current status could not be independently confirmed beyond the emeritus listing.

name: LYNN DUGGAN
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita of Jewelry and Metalsmithing, Nazareth College (Rochester, NY); retired May 2016 after nearly 40 years; continues as a working artist
fc_summary: Lynn Duggan taught jewelry and metalsmithing at Nazareth College (Rochester, NY) for nearly 40 years and retired in May 2016 (now Professor Emerita), marked by the retrospective exhibition "Lynn Duggan: Trajectory." She remains an active artist with a current website and no name change or obituary found.

name: BOB EBENDORF
fc_current_role: Carol Grotnes Belk Distinguished Professor of Art (1999), School of Art and Design, East Carolina University; taught there 1997-2016, now retired/emeritus
fc_summary: Robert "Bob" Ebendorf (b. Sept 30, 1938) is alive and still active as a jeweler/metalsmith. His full/professional name is Robert William Ebendorf ("Bob" is the familiar form, not a name change). He retired from East Carolina University after teaching there 1997-2016, where he held the Carol Grotnes Belk Distinguished Professorship.

name: ALMA EIKERMAN
fc_current_role: Distinguished Professor Emeritus of metalsmithing/jewelry design, Indiana University Bloomington (retired 1978; deceased 1995)
fc_summary: Alma Rosalie Eikerman (1908-1995) was a pioneering American metalsmith and jewelry designer who built the metals program at Indiana University, where she became Distinguished Professor (1976) and retired as Distinguished Professor Emeritus in 1978. She was a founding member of the Society of North American Goldsmiths and died in 1995.

name: HELEN WILLIAMS DRUTT ENGLISH
fc_current_role: Independent curator, gallerist, educator, author, and scholar of modern/contemporary craft and studio jewelry (Helen Drutt Gallery, Philadelphia, founded 1973, closed as physical space 2002). Formerly developed the first US college syllabus on 20th-century crafts at the Philadelphia College of Art (now University of the Arts).
fc_summary: Helen Williams Drutt English (b. Nov 19, 1930), the pioneering Philadelphia craft/jewelry gallerist, curator, and educator, is still living (age 95 as of 2026). The archive listed her as not currently teaching ("n/a"), which is consistent: she has worked as an independent curator/scholar since her gallery closed as a physical space in 2002.

name: CHUCK EVANS
fc_current_role: Professor of Jewelry and Metals, Iowa State University College of Design (1978-2001, retired); founded ISU metals program. Deceased 2015.
fc_summary: Chuck Evans, who founded and led the metals/jewelry program at Iowa State University (1978-2001) and earned his MFA at RIT's School for American Craftsmen, died July 31, 2015 at age 75. No name change.

name: SUSAN EWING
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita of Art, Miami University (Ohio); most recently Director of Cranbrook Academy of Art (named director Jan 2019, no longer director as of ~2025)
fc_summary: Susan R. Ewing, the jeweler/metalsmith, is alive and is now Professor Emerita of Art at Miami University after 35 years (joined 1981, matching the archive). After her Miami career she became Director of Cranbrook Academy of Art (named Jan 2019); she appears to have since stepped down (Cranbrook lists an interim director for 2025).

name: FRED FENSTER
fc_current_role: Professor Emeritus of metalsmithing/jewelry, University of Wisconsin–Madison (retired 2005)
fc_summary: Fred Fenster was the pewter/silver metalsmith and longtime University of Wisconsin–Madison professor (joined 1961, taught 40+ years), retiring in 2005 as Professor Emeritus. He died June 24, 2024.

name: EUGENE KENT BAHLING
fc_current_role: Last known (archived): faculty in jewelry/metalsmithing, Edinboro University of Pennsylvania (listed teaching there since 1969). No current role could be verified; almost certainly long retired given he was born 1942.
fc_summary: Eugene Kent Bahling (b. 1942), archived as a jewelry/metals faculty member at Edinboro University since 1969, has no verifiable current online presence. No faculty page, personal site, obituary, grave record, SNAG profile, or museum-collection entry could be found. Status (alive/deceased, retired) is unknown; if still living he would be about 84 and long retired.

name: PHILIP FIKE
fc_current_role: Professor of metalsmithing/art, Department of Art and Art History, Wayne State University (1953–died in office 1997; 45-year member who built the metals program)
fc_summary: Phillip Fike (the archive's "Philip Fike") was a metalsmith and longtime Wayne State University professor known for reviving the fibula brooch and the niello technique, and a founding member of SNAG. He died December 8, 1997, at age 70.

name: JOSEFA FILOSKY
fc_current_name: Josefa Filkosky (Sister Josefa Filkosky, SC; born Patricia Filkosky)
fc_current_role: Professor of art/sculpture, Seton Hill College (Greensburg, PA), where she taught for 44 years until her death in 1999
fc_summary: The archived "Josefa Filosky" is a misspelling of Josefa Filkosky (1933-1999), a Sister of Charity of Seton Hill and a nationally recognized minimalist sculptor in painted steel who taught at Seton Hill College for 44 years; she died in 1999. Education (Seton Hill, Carnegie Mellon, Cranbrook) and birth year 1933 match exactly.

name: ARLINE M. FISCH
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita of Art, San Diego State University (founded its Jewelry & Metalsmithing program in 1961, retired 2000)
fc_summary: Arline M. Fisch, the pioneering metalsmith who founded SDSU's jewelry and metalsmithing program in 1961, taught there until retiring in 2000 as Professor Emerita, and died on August 20, 2024 at age 93. The archived record correctly identifies her; she is now deceased.

name: ALLAN C. FISHER
fc_current_role: Retired art professor (sculpture/ceramics/metals), Dakota State University, Madison, SD; subsequently active sculptor and volunteer in the Alternatives to Violence Program at a South Dakota penitentiary
fc_summary: Allan C. Fisher (b. 1945) was hired at Dakota State University in 1990 (matching the archive) and retired after about 10 years; he is now a working sculptor in Madison, SD and volunteers with a prison Alternatives to Violence Program. He still maintains his own site, allancfisher.com.

name: ROBERT C. FISHER
fc_current_role: Last known: jewelry/metals instructor, Birmingham Bloomfield Art Association (now Birmingham Bloomfield Art Center), Birmingham, Michigan. Not listed on the current faculty roster.
fc_summary: Could not confirm any current information about this specific Robert C. Fisher (jeweler/metalsmith, b. 1945). The Birmingham Bloomfield Art Association still operates as the Birmingham Bloomfield Art Center, but he is not on its current faculty list (jewelry/metals is now headed by Robin Servo), suggesting he likely left or retired; his current status, possible death, or any name change remain unverified.

name: JOHN T. FIX
fc_current_role: Professor Emeritus, Towson University (Baltimore, MD); headed/directed the Jewelry (Metalsmithing & Jewelry) Department 1967-2000
fc_summary: John T. Fix was the long-time head of the Jewelry/Metalsmithing program at Towson University (1967-2000) and retired as Professor Emeritus. Towson's official Emeriti Directory now marks his name with the asterisk that denotes deceased, so he is likely deceased, though no obituary or death year was found.

name: DR. ELAINE E. FOSTER
fc_current_role: Professor Emerita, Art Department, New Jersey City University (taught there 30+ years; former Department Chairperson). Deceased.
fc_summary: Dr. Elaine E. Foster (full name Elaine Elizabeth Foster, b. ~1934 in Worcester, MA) was a jewelry/metalsmithing artist and Professor Emerita of Art at New Jersey City University; she died October 29, 2024 in New York City. Her name did not change.

name: JEM FREYAULDEHOVEN
fc_current_role: Was professor of jewelry design and silversmithing at Georgia State University, Atlanta (last-known position before death)
fc_summary: Jem W. Freyaldenhoven (1948-1986), a metalsmith/jeweler with a BFA from the Memphis Academy of Arts and an MFA from Tyler School of Art (Temple University), taught jewelry design and silversmithing at Georgia State University in Atlanta. He died in 1986 (reported of AIDS). His sculpture "Krasnaya" is in Georgia's State Art Collection.

name: DANIEL J. FRYE
fc_current_role: Professor of Art and former Art Department Chair (2007-2013), California State University, Sacramento (2000-2014)
fc_summary: Daniel J. Frye (b. 1955) left University of Missouri-Columbia and joined California State University, Sacramento in 2000, where he revitalized the metals/jewelry program and served as Art Department chair (2007-2013). He died in July 2014.

name: GAY GARDNER
fc_summary: No verifiable online record of Gay Gardner as a metalsmith/jeweler could be found. The archived role (teaching metals/jewelry at Spokane Art School since 1990) cannot be confirmed; the Spokane Art School closed in 2008 and reopened as a nonprofit in 2012, and Gardner is not among its current instructors. Status, current role, and whether the name changed are all unknown.

name: MARK BALDRIDGE
fc_current_role: Retired professor of jewelry/metalsmithing, Longwood University (Farmville, VA); retired 2014 after 42 years. Now an independent designer/goldsmith ("architectural jewelry") via Mark Baldridge Design.
fc_summary: Mark Baldridge joined Longwood in 1972 (matching the archive) and taught jewelry/metalsmithing there for 42 years until retiring in 2014; he is alive and active as an independent designer, with his own site referencing a "Waterfall Project 2025."

name: JEFF GEORGANTES
fc_current_role: Jewelry/Metals Instructor and Director of the Rebecca and Mark Byrne Jewelry Studio (formerly Donald Claflin Jewelry Studio), Hopkins Center for the Arts, Dartmouth College, Hanover, NH — since 2005, still active 2025-2026
fc_summary: Jeff Georgantes left College of the Redwoods and has been head of the Jewelry/Metals program at Dartmouth College since 2005, where he is still active as director of the Byrne (formerly Claflin) Jewelry Studio as of the 2025-2026 academic year. He now goes professionally by "T Jeffrey Georgantes."

name: NILDA GETTY
fc_current_role: Retired/former professor of metalsmithing, Colorado State University (Art Department); working studio artist (metalwork, jewelry, prints, photography) in Fort Collins / Loveland, Colorado
fc_summary: Nilda Getty (full name Nilda C. Fernandez Getty, b. 1936) taught metalsmithing at Colorado State University; by 2015 she had left teaching and was a working studio artist in Fort Collins, Colorado. No obituary was found, and a Colorado voter record under "Nilda Fernandez Getty" suggests she remained a Colorado resident, but her current living status is not confirmed.

name: IMOGENE GIELING
fc_current_role: Founder and longtime professor of the metal arts program at San Francisco State University; retired 1990. Also founded UC Berkeley's metal arts department.
fc_summary: Imogene "Tex" Gieling (1923–2024), pioneering Bay Area metalsmith and educator who founded the metal arts departments at UC Berkeley (1956) and San Francisco State University (1965), died December 22, 2024 at 101. She received SNAG's Lifetime Achievement Award in 2003 and endowed the Imogene Gieling Curator of Crafts position at the Oakland Museum of California.

name: DOUGLAS GILCHRIST
fc_current_role: Instructor in Metal-work and Jewelry, Pennsylvania Museum and School of Industrial Art (PMSIA), Philadelphia — now University of the Arts; last known role, active into the early 1940s
